The metastatic carcinoma in the omentum shows a comparable morphology to the tumour present in the breast (C) an in-situ-like structure (arrow) is also identified (D).
in_text_mentions: The nipple biopsy section demonstrated malignant glands and nests with identical histomorphology to the carcinomas described above. The infiltrating carcinoma involved the epidermis, dermis, and deeper parts of the nipple stroma and areolar muscle. Focal epidermal erosion was identified, though the epidermis was devoid of abnormal intraepidermal epithelial clusters. Several malignant cells exhibited cytoplasmic mucinous vacuoles, and dermal lymphovascular invasion was present ( Figure 3 ).

The histology of the primary ovarian tumour was unavailable for review. Subsequent biopsies, displaying identical appearances, revealed multiple metastases to the omentum - the largest tumour deposit being 5 cm, pelvic peritoneum, bilateral sides of the diaphragm, liver capsule and gallbladder bed, including to the serosa, muscularis propria and mucosa of the sigmoid colon. The basement membrane-like matrix with occasional basal stretched-out cells were also noted in the section of metastatic carcinoma to the omentum and pelvic peritoneum ( Figure 3B ).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E histology of metastatic ovarian mucinous carcinoma involving the ileocecal valve, with mucinous features as described in the caption and in-text correlation. B: CK20 immunohistochemistry of metastatic ovarian mucinous carcinoma; tumor glands are negative while residual colonic glands are positive, supporting the diagnosis. C: CK7 immunohistochemistry showing diffuse positivity in tumor cells and negativity in residual colonic glands, consistent with metastatic ovarian mucinous carcinoma. D: Pancytokeratin immunohistochemistry demonstrating positivity in both normal colonic glands and tumor glands, confirming epithelial origin.

CK7 positive - reverse pattern, tumor showing positive features, and residual colonic glands are negative (4x). D. Pancytokeratin positive for both normal colonic glands and tumor glands (4x).
in_text_mentions: a large ovarian mass and peritoneal carcinomatosis. At this time, the pathology report was amended to include specific immunohistochemistry (IHC) assays. These described the mucinous features of the uncommon ileocecal ulcer. The tumor cells were positive for pancytokeratin and had a diffuse expression of cytokeratin 7 (CK7). They were partially positive (up to 20%) for CK20 and CDX2 but negative for estrogen receptors (ER), monoclonal carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), and synaptophysin. This immunophenotypic pattern is strongly consistent with a metastatic mucinous ovarian carcinoma (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E section shows a cystic mucinous ovarian tumor with a distinct nodule, consistent with the captioned ovarian mucinous carcinoma case. B: H&E panel shows mucinous borderline morphology adjacent to a signet-ring cell nodule, directly matching the ovarian mucinous carcinoma caption. C: High-power H&E shows signet-ring cells with intracytoplasmic mucin, a distinctive feature of this rare ovarian mucinous carcinoma case. D: H&E panel shows foci of infiltrative invasion in the ovarian mucinous carcinoma, consistent with carcinoma histology.

D) Foci of infiltrative invasion (H&E 100x).

A: Colonoscopy image showing an ileocecal sessile erythematous friable plaque in a case report titled metastatic ovarian mucinous carcinoma presenting as ileocecal adenocarcinoma; the lesion is the patient manifestation, but no configured ovarian mucinous carcinoma vocabulary finding applies. B: Colonoscopy image during biopsy of the same ileocecal metastatic lesion in the ovarian mucinous carcinoma case report; no configured vocabulary finding applies. C: Colonoscopy image of the same ileocecal lesion after biopsies in the ovarian mucinous carcinoma case report; no configured vocabulary finding applies.

panels.figure_caption: Second colonoscopy A. A 2-cm erythematous friable sessile plaque was noted on the cephalad margins of the ileocecal valve (consistent with a 0-IIa type lesion-Paris classification). B. Biopsy instrumentation, continued friable erythema of ileocecal valve. C. Sessile plaque after several biopsies were taken. Moderate friability.
in_text_mentions: The tissue specimen obtained during colonoscopy required a repeat biopsy in order to exclude malignancy. A second colonoscopy confirmed the initial suspicion of poorly differentiated, invasive colon adenocarcinoma with partial mucinous features (Figure 2).
